sutta: is 4.4.36 on a certain occasion the exalted one was journeying along the high road between ukata and satavia now the brahman dhona was also journeying along the high road between ukata and satabia then the brahmin dhona beheld on the footprints of the exalted one the real mouse with a thousand spokes with their rims and hubs and all their attributes complete on seeing these he thought thus it is wonderful indeed it is marvellous indeed these will not be the footprints of one in human form just then the exalted one stepped aside from the high road and sat down at the root of a certain tree sitting cross-legged beholding holding his body upright and setting up mindfulness in front of him then the brahmin donor following up the exalted one's footprints beheld the exalted one seated at the foot of a certain tree seeing him comely faith inspiring with senses calmed tranquil of mine in the attainment of composure by mastery control like a tamed alert perfectly trained elephant he approached the exalted one and drawing near to him said this your worship will be a deva and the buddha said no indeed brahman i am not a deva then your worship will be a gandaba no indeed brahman i am not a gandaba indeed brahman not ayaka then your worship will be a human being no indeed brahman i'm not a human being and brahman said when questioned thus your worship will be a deva a gandaba a yaka a human being you reply not so brahmin i'm not a deva a gandaba a yaka i'm not a human being who then pray will your worship be and the buddha said brahman those are savas whereby if they were not abandoned i should become a deva those asavas in me are abandoned cut off at the root made like a palm tree stump made non-existent of a nature not to arise again in future time those are savas whereby if they were not abandoned i should become a gandaba a yaka a human being those asavas in me are abandoned not to arise again in future time just as brahmin a lotus in blue red or white no born in the water grown up in the water when it reaches the surface stands there and soil by the water just so brahmin though born in the world grown up in the world having overcome the world i abide unsoiled by the world take it that i am a buddha brahmin this is one of those well-known sutas where this man because of seeing the footprints of the buddha these brahmins they like to observe all these marks of the human body you know and from observing the footprints of the buddha he said there must be something special about this person so he asked the buddha whether he was a deva a heavenly being and whether he was a gandaba a tree spirit a yaka another type of spiritual being a human being etc and the buddha said he was not any one of those but the buddha meant is that the buddha has no more ego no more self and because he has no more self he does not see himself as a human being he sees all beings as one with him and in fact he sees the whole world now like a dream he's mentioned somewhere else buddha comes from the word buddhi buddhi means knowledge or wisdom so the buddha is an enlightened one no more self no more ego the buddha said monks possessed of four qualities a man is incapable of falling away he is near to nibana what are the four herein among is perfect in virtue he is guarded as to the doors of the sense faculties he is moderate in eating he is given to watchfulness or wakefulness and in what way is among perfect in virtue hearing among is virtuous he dwells restrained with the restraint of the patimoka the code of preception for among perfect in the practice of right conduct he sees danger in the slightest faults he takes up and trains himself in the stages of training thus among is perfect in virtue and how is a man guarded as to the doors of the sense faculties hearing among seeing an object with the eye does not grasp at the general features or at the details thereof since coveting and dejection evil and profitable states might flow in upon one who dwells with the faculty of the eye unrestrained he applies himself to such restraint he sets a guard over the faculty of the eye attains restrained thereof when he hears a features or details thereof but since coveting and dejection evil and profitable states might flow in upon one who dwells with his senses unrestrained he applies himself to such restraint he sets a guard over the sense doors attains restraint thereof that is how a monk has the doors of the sense faculty's garden and how is among moderate in eating herein a monk takes his food thoughtfully and prudently not for sport not for indulgence not for personal charm or adornment but just enough for the support for the continuance of the body for its resting unharmed to help the living of the holy life with this thought my former feeling i checked and i set going no new feeling thus maintenance shall be mine blamelessness and comfort in life thus is among moderate in eating and how is among given to watchfulness or wakefulness by day a monk walks up and down and then sits thus cleansing his heart of conditions that should be checked by night for the first watch he does likewise in the middle watch of the night lying on his right side he takes up the lion posture resting one foot on the other and thus collected and composed fixes his thoughts on rising up again in the last watch of the night at early dawn he walks up and down then sits and so cleanses his heart of conditions that should be checked that is how among is given to watchfulness possess of these four qualities among
